title: Mocking and Test Utilities
description: Mocking TypeScript React components, typing test utilities, and using jest.mock with types.

data.text: Mocking in TypeScript requires understanding both Jest's mocking mechanisms and TypeScript's type system. When you mock a module, TypeScript needs to know the shape of the mock so you get proper autocomplete and type safety.

data.title: Type Safety in Mocks
data.text: Untyped mocks can silently accept wrong arguments or return wrong shapes, leading to tests that pass but hide bugs. TypeScript catches these issues at compile time.

cards.title: jest.mock()
cards.description: Automatically mocks an entire module. Best for external dependencies like API clients.

cards.title: jest.fn()
cards.description: Creates a manually controlled mock function. Best for functions you need to assert on.

cards.title: MSW (Mock Service Worker)
cards.description: Intercepts network requests at the service worker level. Best for API mocking.

items.text: Type the mock with jest.MockedFunction or jest.MockedClass
items.hint: Preserves the original type for type safety

items.text: Use __esModule: true for ES module interop
items.hint: Required when mocking ES modules with Jest

items.text: Type the return values of mockResolvedValue
items.hint: Cast to the expected interface or use 'as'
Only mock external dependencies, not your own components

data.title: Exercise: Mock a Custom Hook
data.description: Create a typed mock for the useCounter custom hook from the Typing Hooks module.
steps: Create a jest.MockedFunction for the hook
Set up mockReturnValue to control counter behavior
Write a test component that uses the mocked hook
Assert the component renders the mocked counter values
data.expectedOutcome: A test suite where the custom hook is fully typed and controllable through mocks.

items.question: Why does jest.mock need __esModule?
items.answer: ES modules use named exports while CommonJS uses default exports. The __esModule flag tells Jest to respect the original export structure.

items.question: Should I type mocks with 'as any'?
items.answer: Avoid 'as any' when possible. Use jest.MockedFunction<typeof fn> to preserve types. Only fall back to 'as any' for third-party libraries with poor type definitions.

items.question: How do I mock React Router?
items.answer: Use MemoryRouter with initialEntries for routing tests, or mock useNavigate and useParams with jest.fn() returning typed values.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Mock components by typing their props
Create custom render utilities for shared setup
data.takeaway: Typed mocks make your tests safer and easier to debug.
